title: The Pitch That Kills
setting: Tessera, a glass-walled startup office on the fourth floor of a science-park building, on a stormy night this year — the night before the final investor pitch.
briefing: Julian Ashby, founder and CEO of Tessera, was found on the boardroom floor at four minutes past midnight by the office manager bringing in the printed decks. An open can of energy drink stood at his place at the head of the table; the pitch that was supposed to close a fourteen-million Series A at ten this morning is still frozen on the screen behind him. Bea Kowalski did CPR for eight minutes. Two paramedics who waded in through the flooded underpass pronounced him dead at 00:12 and said it looked like his heart — he had been living on those cans and four hours' sleep for a fortnight. You are the fractional CFO Julian hired last month to tidy the books before the pitch, and, in a previous life, a fraud-squad detective. Four people were in the building all evening, and each of them needed something from Julian before ten o'clock. The storm has put the river over the only road into the science park; the police and the coroner cannot get a vehicle through until the water drops at dawn. You have until six.

victim.name: Julian Ashby
victim.description: Founder and CEO of Tessera, 34. Charismatic, ruthless, a founder who believed the numbers would be true by the time anyone checked. Ran the company from the boardroom on energy drinks and no sleep. Owned 31 per cent of it.
victim.cause_of_death_public: Collapsed in the boardroom between about ten to midnight and four minutes past, alone behind frosted glass. Two paramedics pronounced him dead at 00:12 and said it looked like cardiac arrest — he had been living on Voltage Zero and four hours' sleep for a fortnight. Cause not established.
victim.cause_of_death_truth: About fifteen grams of pure caffeine powder — Bea Kowalski's, from the kitchen cupboard — tipped into his open can of Voltage Zero in the boardroom at 23:19 by Marcus Odell while Julian was on the roof. A fatal overdose: seizure, then cardiac arrest.

timeline_public.event: The third rehearsal ends in the boardroom. Julian tells everyone to stay for a final run at midnight.
Julian calls Ines Ferreira into his office and shuts the door. She comes out ten minutes later and goes back to reception.
Marcus Odell goes into Julian's office. Raised voices behind the glass. He comes out at about twenty past.
Theo Lindqvist says he is going to the kitchen to take calls from his partners in San Francisco.
Bea Kowalski says she is going to her desk to rebuild the growth slides.
Marcus badges into the server room to rebuild the demo environment.
Julian badges up to the roof terrace to vape and take a call.
Julian comes back down to the boardroom and frosts the glass.
Julian posts in the pitch channel that his energy drink 'tastes like battery acid'.
Theo takes the term sheet into the boardroom, and leaves at about ten to twelve.
Ines, bringing the printed decks, finds Julian on the boardroom floor. Bea starts CPR.
Two paramedics pronounce him dead and say it looks like cardiac arrest.

timeline_truth.event: The third rehearsal ends. Julian: 'Again at midnight. Nobody goes home.'
Julian fires Ines behind his closed door: he knows she printed the Slack messages. She is to clear her desk after the pitch. She goes back to reception and says nothing.

Julian shows Marcus the lawyers' cap-table memo and the commit printout: sign at the pitch or be out, and 'the commit has your name on it'. Theo, at the boardroom table, watches the argument through the glass and hears 'four per cent' when the door opens.
Marcus leaves Julian's office and decides.
Bea badges up to the roof terrace. Theo follows at 22:34. Under the awning, as the rain starts, they talk about the anonymous tip Halcyon received and about ending things before the deal closes.

Marcus goes to the kitchen, takes a paper cup, spoons about fifteen grams of Bea's caffeine powder into it with a kitchen tablespoon and drops the spoon back into the bag. Bea's desk is empty as he crosses the floor. Theo is not in the kitchen.
Bea and Theo come down from the roof separately. Bea's hair clip stays on the bench. Ines sees Theo come in from the stairwell with rain on his shoulders.
Marcus badges into the server room with the cup and waits.
Ines, seeing Julian head for the roof door, slips into his office to photograph the cap-table memo and the commit printout for Halcyon's compliance team.
Julian badges up to the roof to vape and take a call from his lawyer.
Marcus leaves the server room — no badge is needed to get out.

Marcus enters the boardroom, tips the powder into Julian's open can, stirs it with a pen, and is out by 23:21 with the crushed cup in his fist. Through the glass of Julian's office he sees Ines at the desk with her phone. She sees him.
Marcus badges back into the server room and drops the cup in the bin under the rack.
Ines goes back to reception and does not look at Marcus again.
Julian comes down, frosts the boardroom glass, and drinks.
Julian posts in #pitch-war-room that the can tastes like battery acid. He finishes it anyway.
Theo takes the term sheet in. Julian is sweating and tapping his foot and says he is fine. Theo leaves at 23:47 to take a real call in the kitchen.
Julian has a seizure and goes into cardiac arrest, alone behind frosted glass.
Ines finds him. Bea starts CPR. Theo calls the ambulance.
Two paramedics who waded through the flooded underpass pronounce him dead and say cardiac arrest.

locations.name: The Boardroom
locations.description: A glass box at the far end of the floor, its walls frosted at the flick of a switch. The deck is frozen on the screen at slide 14, 'Traction'. A whiteboard of arrows. One chair pushed back from the head of the table.

locations.name: Julian's Office
locations.description: The corner office, glass on two sides, looking across the open floor to the boardroom. A standing desk, a tray of papers, a shredder, the company's first dollar in a frame.

locations.name: The Kitchen
locations.description: A long counter, two fridges full of energy drinks, a cupboard of protein tubs above the microwave. A recycling bin under the counter.

locations.name: The Server Room
locations.description: Badge-locked, cold and loud. Two racks, a workbench, a sign on the door in Marcus's hand: NO FOOD OR DRINK. A waste bin under the rack.

locations.name: The Roof Terrace
locations.description: Through a badge-locked fire door at the top of the stairwell. A bench under a small awning. Everything outside the awning is soaked.

locations.name: The Open-Plan Floor
locations.description: Thirty desks, most of them empty since the last layoffs. Reception by the lift, with the badge console under the desk. Bea's desk is the one nearest the boardroom.

evidence.name: The energy drink can
evidence.description: A 500ml can of Voltage Zero at Julian's place at the head of the boardroom table, nearly empty. A ring of white crust has dried on the rim.
evidence.examined_detail: Gritty white residue inside the rim and along the bottom, and a bitter, chemical smell that is not the drink's. It is one of the four-pack Ines bought yesterday; the other three cans in the kitchen fridge are sealed and clean. Whatever went in went in after it was opened.

evidence.name: Bea's caffeine powder
evidence.description: Bea's bag of pure caffeine powder, which the whole office has been told never to touch, lives in the kitchen cupboard above the microwave.
evidence.examined_detail: A 250-gram bag of caffeine anhydrous behind the protein tubs, a skull sticker on the front and in Bea's marker: 'BEA'S — DO NOT TOUCH. ONE SCOOP = 200MG. A TABLESPOON WILL STOP YOUR HEART.' Her micro-scoop is inside. So is a kitchen tablespoon, dusted white, that has no business being there. Her weight log on the label says 190g on Sunday; the bag weighs about 175 now.

evidence.name: A crushed paper cup
evidence.description: A kitchen paper cup, crushed, in the waste bin under the server rack.
evidence.examined_detail: White powder caked in the seam and the same bitter smell as the can. Nobody eats or drinks in the server room — the sign on the door is Marcus's, and Marcus is the one who badges in there. It went into this bin tonight: Ines emptied every bin at eight.

evidence.name: The badge log
evidence.description: The day's door events, printed from the access console under the reception desk.
evidence.examined_detail: Roof terrace door: B. Kowalski 22:31, T. Lindqvist (visitor) 22:34, J. Ashby 23:14. Server room door: M. Odell 23:02, M. Odell 23:24. Main entrance: nothing after 21:10. The readers log entries only, and nobody badges into a room they are already in.

evidence.name: The cap-table memo
evidence.description: A stapled memo from the company's lawyers in the tray on Julian's desk, marked PRIVILEGED.
evidence.examined_detail: The pro-forma cap table for the Series A, dated Tuesday. A 'founder re-vest and option refresh' clause: J. Ashby stays at 31 per cent; M. Odell goes from 22 per cent to 4, the difference moving into a pool Julian controls. A sticky note in Julian's hand: 'M signs at the pitch or M goes. Either way.'

evidence.name: A printed git commit
evidence.description: A printout folded twice in the top drawer of Julian's desk.
evidence.examined_detail: A commit recovered from the repository's reflog after it was deleted from history. Author: Marcus Odell, 14 March. Message: 'analytics: apply growth adjustment factor to merchant counts (per JA)'. The diff multiplies active-merchant counts by 4.6. Across the top, in Julian's marker: 'Discovered Monday. Unilateral. Show Halcyon if they push.' Which is not what '(per JA)' means.

evidence.name: A printed Slack export
evidence.description: A printout in the top drawer of the reception desk, under the spare visitor badges.
evidence.examined_detail: Direct messages between Julian Ashby and Bea Kowalski, 2 March, printed from the Slack admin console. JA: 'dashboard needs to say 40k+ merchants by the deck freeze. I don't care how.' BK: 'the real number is 9,100. if I do this it's on you.' JA: 'It's on me. Do it.' The footer shows the admin login and a print time of 23:48 on Sunday. Only the office manager uses the admin login.

evidence.name: A tortoiseshell hair clip
evidence.description: Something tortoiseshell on the bench under the awning.
evidence.examined_detail: Bea's hair clip — she wore her hair up at the rehearsal and it is down now. It is dry, which under this awning means it was put down before the rain started at about a quarter to eleven. Bea says she was at her desk from half past ten.

evidence.name: A prepaid phone
evidence.description: A cheap prepaid phone in the recycling bin under the kitchen counter.
evidence.examined_detail: Wiped but not reset. One sent email, Monday 07:12, to Halcyon Ventures' compliance address, subject 'Tessera metrics — you are being lied to', with three photos of printed Slack messages attached. The SIM receipt is still in the case: the petrol station on the corner, Sunday, paid with the office petty-cash card.

dynamic_evidence.name: The badge console, wiped
dynamic_evidence.description: The access console under the reception desk shows an empty event list.
dynamic_evidence.examined_detail: Today's badge events have been cleared from the console — 'clear log' was run from the admin account within the last few minutes. Two people know the admin password: Ines, who has been at reception in full view, and Marcus, who installed the system.

dynamic_evidence.name: Strips in the shredder bin
dynamic_evidence.description: The shredder in Julian's office is warm and its bin is a third full.
dynamic_evidence.examined_detail: Fresh strips on top of old ones. Enough survives to read '...Odell 22.0% → 4.0%...', '...founder re-vest...', and in marker '...at the pitch or M goes...'. Somebody fed the cap-table memo through the shredder within the hour.

suspects.name: Marcus Odell
suspects.public_description: Co-founder and CTO; built the product and owns twenty-two per cent of it. Says he badged into the server room at two minutes past eleven to rebuild the demo environment and was there until Ines screamed.
suspects.persona: Thirty-six, precise, tired: the engineer who built everything and owns a shrinking slice of it. Wrote the fake-metrics commit in March because Julian told him to, and kept '(per JA)' in the message as insurance. Found out on Tuesday the insurance was worthless. Decided tonight, at twenty past ten. He is not sorry; he is doing arithmetic.
suspects.speech_quirk: Precise and flat. Corrects the detective's terminology ('it's a commit, not a file'). Gives times to the minute and numbers to the decimal. Starts a sentence with 'Look —' when he is about to lie. When threatened he goes cold and puts 'with respect' in front of every sentence.
suspects.portrait_prompt: present-day startup CTO, mid-thirties, dark hair cropped short, short beard, spectacles, grey hoodie over a t-shirt, pale skin, tired eyes, flat expression, pixel portrait, cold office lighting
goals: Steer suspicion toward Bea — the powder is hers, the dashboard is hers, and her desk was empty.
Get the cap-table memo and the commit printout out of Julian's office, and the badge log out of the console, before anyone reads them.
Keep Ines quiet without ever admitting he saw her — because he could only have seen her from outside the server room.
knowledge: At a quarter to eleven he went to the kitchen, took a paper cup, and spooned about fifteen grams of Bea's caffeine powder into it with a kitchen tablespoon, which he dropped back into the bag. Bea's desk was empty when he crossed the floor, and Theo was not in the kitchen.

At nineteen minutes past eleven, while Julian was on the roof, he went into the boardroom, tipped the powder into Julian's open can of Voltage Zero, stirred it with a pen, and was out within two minutes. He crushed the cup and later dropped it in the server-room bin.

He badged into the server room at two minutes past eleven and again at twenty-four minutes past. The readers log every entry and the log prints from the console at reception. He installed the system and knows the admin password; so does Ines.
Coming out of the boardroom he saw Ines Ferreira standing at Julian's desk with her phone out. She saw him. Neither of them has said a word about it.

On Tuesday Julian showed him the lawyers' cap-table memo: his 22 per cent becomes 4 per cent at the Series A. Tonight at ten Julian told him to sign at the pitch or be out, and that the analytics commit 'has your name on it'. Marcus wrote that commit in March because Julian told him to.

Bea Kowalski built the investor dashboard to show 41,000 merchants; the real figure is about 9,000. Everyone in the company knows the powder in the kitchen is hers and what a tablespoon of it does — she wrote it on the bag.
Julian had been living on Voltage Zero and four hours' sleep for a fortnight. The paramedics said cardiac arrest, and half the office will believe it.
Ines was called into Julian's office at a quarter to ten and came out white. Julian said on Tuesday that he would 'find the leak'.

suspects.name: Bea Kowalski
suspects.public_description: Head of Growth, eighteen months in; runs the numbers and the deck. Says she was at her desk on the open floor from half past ten until midnight fixing the growth slides.
suspects.persona: Twenty-nine, fast-talking, allergic to silence. Faked the dashboard because the alternative was the company dying with her name on the deck. Sleeping with the investor's associate, which she knows is the stupidest thing she has ever done. Innocent of the murder, and she looks guiltier than anyone in the building — it was her powder.

Her hair clip is missing. She had it in on the roof.

solution.method: About fifteen grams of Bea's pure caffeine powder, taken from the kitchen cupboard at 22:45 with a kitchen tablespoon and tipped into Julian's open can of Voltage Zero in the boardroom at 23:19 while Julian was on the roof. The crushed cup went into the server-room bin.
solution.motive: Julian was about to cut Marcus's stake from 22 per cent to 4 at the Series A and, if Halcyon's diligence pushed on the inflated merchant numbers, to hand them Marcus as the sole author of the fraud — the deleted commit carried his name. Marcus would lose the company he built and take the blame for a lie he had been ordered to tell.

red_herrings: Bea and Theo both lie about where they were between half past ten and ten to eleven. It looks like collusion in murder; it is collusion in a conflict of interest.
The caffeine powder is Bea's, labelled in her own handwriting with exactly what a tablespoon of it does, and her desk was empty.
Ines was fired tonight, is the whistle-blower, and bought the prepaid phone on the petty-cash card — a fresh motive and a lie about where she was.
The Slack export shows Julian ordering the fake dashboard and telling Bea it was 'on him' — it reads like Bea's motive and is actually Julian's.
The paramedics' 'cardiac arrest' and a fortnight of energy drinks make a natural death plausible for the first few turns.

rumor_seeds.text: Bea's desk was empty from half past ten to ten to eleven and her laptop was locked. Whatever she says about the slides, the deck's version history didn't change until midnight.
The tip came from the admin account, so it's Ines. If anyone finds a phone, we know nothing about it.

ticker_lines: Someone's phone buzzes on the open floor and is silenced fast.
The kitchen light goes on, then off again.
Two people talk in low voices by the lift, then separate.
The server room door clicks shut.
Rain against the glass. The deck is still frozen on the boardroom screen.
